reviews.x: Love these brushes! We own two because I have one curly headed child and one with very thin straight hair.  They both want to keep their hair long.  However, prior to our purchase, brushing was a nightmare of whining and suicidal thoughts (on my part).  I'm not sure how the brush works, but I do know that my daughter stopped fuzzing!  I can comb her long locks without tears, which makes me very happy!  And, as a bonus, their hair looks great!!!!

I just got mine in the mail and used it right away. I have a nightmare of thick and wavy hair, and spent most of last night tossing and turning. Basically, it looked like one of those kitchen scratch pads in a lovely shade of auburn in the back. This brush got that mess out in no time, with just a little tugging and pulling. While it's in no way "pain free," it's a huge step forward. Whoever designed this brush, (Mr. Mercier?) deserves a high five... or a fist bump... or whatever the kid

I have fine hair that knots up and tangles constantly.  Washing my hair is so unpleasant even with conditioner and leave-in de-tangling solution. This is better than a wide-tooth comb. Gently goes through tangles and knots with minimal hair loss.  Buying another one to keep in my purse.

claims.text: Many reviewers say the brush detangles hair painlessly and effectively, especially for children with fine or tangly hair.
A common complaint is that the brush fails to detangle and does nothing for knots.
Several reviewers describe the brush as cheaply made, comparing it to a Barbie or dollar-store brush, with bristles breaking or melting.
Some reviewers report the brush pulls or hurts the hair rather than gliding through it.

qa.q: Will this brush work for my hair type?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on hair type suitability: one reviewer says it worked for both a curly-haired child and a child with very thin straight hair [4], while others report it failed on very fine long hair [1] and thick hair [2]. Several reviewers also say it does not help with tangled hair [3][5].

claims.text: It worked for both a curly-haired child and a child with very thin straight hair [4].
It was like using a Barbie brush on very fine long hair [1].
It was hard and inflexible for a thick-haired child [2].
It does not help with tangled hair [3][5].

qa.q: Does it pull or hurt when detangling?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree: some report pulling or pain, while others say it detangles well. One reviewer says it pulls her hair out [2], and another says the hard, inflexible bristles make a tender-headed child scream [6]; however, a five-star reviewer calls it the answer to hours of detangling for long thick hair [4].
